name: timechange
resume: CRAN timechange 0.4.0 is translated. Civil arithmetic follows the bundled CCTZ normalization. Time zones are Python zoneinfo, which reads the same system zoneinfo files. A skipped civil time inverts CCTZ pre and post.

functions.name: time_add
functions.done: Civil addition through zoneinfo. A skipped hour uses the post-transition offset when roll_dst is post.

check.case: 2010-03-14 01:02:03 America/New_York plus 1 hour and 50 minutes, roll_dst post

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(timechange))
stopifnot(packageDescription("timechange")$Version == "0.4.0")

x <- as.POSIXct("2010-03-14 01:02:03", tz = "America/New_York")
one <- function() time_add(x, hours = 1, minutes = 50, roll_dst = "post")
warm <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time()); one(); elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf("%.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))
cat(sprintf("%.17g", unclass(warm)), "\n")
proof.python:
import statistics
import time
from timechange import (
    time_add, time_at_tz, time_ceiling, time_clock_at_tz, time_floor,
    time_force_tz, time_get, time_round, time_subtract, time_update,
)
from timechange.civil import Posixct

x = Posixct(1268546523, "America/New_York")
def one():
    return time_add(x, hour=1, minute=50, roll_dst="post")
warm = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter(); one(); elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print("%.17g" % statistics.median(elapsed))
got = [float(warm.seconds)]
print(got if isinstance(got, str) else " ".join("%.17g" % v for v in got))

functions.name: time_subtract
functions.done: Subtraction negates the periods and calls time_add.
